title: Boteh
subtitle: بته‌جقه · boteh-jegheh · 彎尖水滴紋（描述性暫譯）

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Look for a rounded body with a bent, pointed tip. The Getty vocabulary relates this form to paisley.

sections.title: Similar motifs and how to tell them apart

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Compare the closed outline with an open branching scroll. Trace the whole shape before naming it.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: The term is used across carpets and other textiles; it is not a location certificate.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: No object-specific symbolic intention is established by these selected notes. This is a limit of this Wiki, not proof that meanings never existed. Do not attach a universal meaning to a visual match.

title: Herati / Mahi
subtitle: هراتی / ماهی‌درهم · herāti / māhi darham · 赫拉特式魚形葉重複圖案（暫譯）

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Identify the whole repeat: diamond, central flower and surrounding curved leaves.

sections.title: Similar motifs and how to tell them apart

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: One curved leaf is insufficient. Compare the arrangement of neighbouring units, not just one cropped detail.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Farahan is one documented association in the Qajar survey, not an exclusive origin.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: No object-specific symbolic intention is established by these selected notes. This is a limit of this Wiki, not proof that meanings never existed. Do not attach a universal meaning to a visual match.

title: Shah Abbasi palmette
subtitle: شاه‌عباسی · shāh-abbāsi · 沙阿阿巴斯式扇形花紋（暫譯）

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Palmette: a stylized fan-like flower. “Shah Abbasi” can also describe a broader floral pattern.

sections.title: Similar motifs and how to tell them apart

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Do not label every flower Shah Abbasi. Read the floral unit together with the surrounding design.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: The Royal Collection description combines Shah Abbas palmettes and islimi vines in one carpet.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: No object-specific symbolic intention is established by these selected notes. This is a limit of this Wiki, not proof that meanings never existed. Do not attach a universal meaning to a visual match.

title: Islimi / arabesque
subtitle: اسلیمی · eslimi / islimi · 卷草紋（描述性暫譯）

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Follow the branching scroll rather than isolating one flower. The Met example has broad blue bands among smaller flowers.

sections.title: Similar motifs and how to tell them apart

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: A palmette is a floral unit; an arabesque is a scrolling vegetal arrangement. Both may appear together.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: The Met labels its seventeenth-century example “probably Iran.” Its attribution has been debated.

claims.label: Uncertain

title: Toranj and Lachak
subtitle: ترنج و لچک · toranj va lachak · 中央團花與角隅紋（暫譯）

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Read the centre and corners together. This page concerns composition, not one small repeated flower.

sections.title: Similar motifs and how to tell them apart

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: A medallion can contain many smaller motifs. Identify layout before describing those details.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: The Ardabil Carpet is a dated museum example with a central medallion and corner portions.

claims.label: Interpretation
claims.text: The V&A presents alternative explanations for its unequal lamps, not proof of a universal medallion meaning. The page does not name the individual proposers.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: A similar layout cannot establish date, origin or intended symbolism for another carpet.

title: Rug structure
subtitle: Read the layout before the details.

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Find the field, then main border, minor borders and separating guards. These terms locate a feature.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Warp: lengthwise foundation threads. Weft: crosswise threads. Pile: projecting cut knot ends. These describe construction, not decoration.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: Neither a knot name nor a design name independently proves geographical origin.

title: What makes a rug valuable?
subtitle: A documentation guide for collectors, not an appraisal.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Record the fibre of pile and foundation separately. A silk label alone is not a monetary valuation.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Record a unit and method. Density can enable detail, but the Wiki supplies no price conversion or universal quality ranking.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Document testing where available. Screen colour cannot establish dye chemistry. Natural versus synthetic is not a simple value scale.

claims.label: Observation
claims.text: Describe visible losses and consult a condition report. A fragment cannot be treated as an intact original composition.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Use dated inscriptions or documented analysis. Cleveland’s fragment shows why a convincing style can still require revised dating.

claims.label: Historical claim
claims.text: Provenance means documented ownership history. Retain gaps and questioned transfers.

claims.label: Uncertain
claims.text: Motif alone does not determine value. These sources document characteristics; they do not establish prices or weights for an appraisal algorithm.
